content:
**Visual analysis of test image:**
- Affected part: corn ear (cob)
- Yellow kernels with white/grayish cottony mycelial growth running between kernel rows and concentrated at the tip
- No pink/red coloration (rules out Gibberella)
- No green coloration (rules out Trichoderma)
- No olive/yellow-green powdery spores (rules out Aspergillus)

**Comparison with Ear_rots_Diplodia reference:**
- Both show white/gray cottony mycelium on corn ear
- Diplodia reference shows heavier bleaching/browning of kernels — test image kernels are more vibrant yellow (possibly earlier infection stage)
- The white thread-like growth between kernel rows matches Diplodia's characteristic dense white mycelium

The white (not pink, not green) mycelial growth on the corn ear strongly points to **Ear_rots_Diplodia**.
